answer: The network can audit declared capacity: each identity publicly posts its compute power, and the network sizes work to that claim, then spot-checks a random sample with simultaneous burst tasks - a flash flood down the ridge that only real capacity survives. One willow bends honestly and passes. A sybil farmer claiming a thousand capacities from one machine faces copper-hard math: burst tasks for all fakes arrive at once, each missing proof slashes its stake, and under-capacity identities are delisted. Faking one identity passes; faking a thousand fails its own declared audit.
